logging.notes: On by default. Every request carries the io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel _meta key, info unless serverLogLevel says otherwise, which is how a 2026-07-28 server is asked for logs. A notifications/message is written to the Mastra logger at a mapped level and passed to the entry's logger callback. enableServerLogs: false removes the key and the handler.

instructions.notes: Read on connect and returned by getServerInstructions(). They are added to the agent's system prompt, under a heading naming the server, only when the entry sets forwardInstructions: true, and are cut to 512 characters unless instructionsMaxLength says otherwise.

icons.notes: Not rendered or validated by @mastra/mcp. getServerInfo() returns the server's Implementation as sent, icons and websiteUrl included, and its comment says the URLs are not validated. Tool icons are not copied into the Mastra tool or the serialisable definition.

tasks.notes: Off by default. tasks: true on a server entry declares the io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension (SEP-2663). A tools/call answered with resultType task is polled with tasks/get until it ends, and the final CallToolResult becomes the tool result. An input_required task is answered through inputRequests with tasks/update, or suspends the tool call when there is no handler. Aborting the call or reaching maxWaitMs sends tasks/cancel. mcp.tasks exposes get, update and cancel. The SDK rejects a task result, so Mastra rewrites it on the transport before the SDK parses it.

list.notes: tasks/list is not sent. The methods used are tasks/get, tasks/update and tasks/cancel.

cancel.notes: Sent on abort, at maxWaitMs, and through mcp.tasks.cancel(). Only with tasks enabled on the entry.

jsonSchema.notes: A tool schema with no $schema is treated as 2020-12. Draft-07 is accepted as is. A 2019-09 schema is converted to 2020-12 when that can be done faithfully, and passed through unchanged when not. An input schema over 128 levels or 10,000 nodes, or one that fails a draft-07-based meta-schema check, drops the tool from the list. Output is validated by the SDK's Ajv validator unless the entry passes a jsonSchemaValidator. Which keywords the validators honour was not read.

io.modelcontextprotocol/ui.notes: Declared with an empty settings object on every connection, with no option to leave it out. @mastra/mcp renders nothing. It keeps tool and result _meta, stamps ui.serverId next to ui.resourceUri, and withholds tools whose _meta.ui.visibility lacks model. The renderer is Studio (packages/playground-ui), which an application built on Agent and MCPClient alone does not have.

evidence.note: The clientCapabilities sent with server/discover and every later request were {"extensions":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/ui":{}}} (wire.jsonl). The probe ran @mastra/mcp 2.9.0-alpha.1; the capability code is the same at bb984550.

io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks.notes: Declared with an empty settings object only when the server entry sets tasks. See the tasks row.

io.modelcontextprotocol/events.notes: Application API for the draft MCP Events extension (SEP-3415). mcp.events.list() sends events/list, and subscribe() delivers occurrences by webhook (events/subscribe) when the client has a webhook option, else push (events/stream), else poll (events/poll), from the modes the event advertises. Nothing is declared in the client capabilities; the client reads the server's io.modelcontextprotocol/events entry. createMCPEventsTools gives a model mcp_events_list, mcp_events_subscribe and mcp_events_unsubscribe.

modelInitiatedResourceRead.notes: No tool gives the model resources/read. The only model-facing tools @mastra/mcp builds are the server's own tools and the optional MCP Events tools.

protocolEraForcing.notes: protocolVersion on a server entry takes '2026-07-28', which pins that revision with no fallback, or 'legacy', which runs the initialize handshake with no probe. Omitted, the client probes and falls back. getServerProtocolVersions() reports what was negotiated. A successful verdict is reused on reconnect and dropped after a failed connect.

toolAnnotationPolicies.notes: The function form of requireToolApproval receives the server's tool annotations, placed so a caller cannot override them. After a transport failure in mid-call, a tool annotated readOnlyHint or idempotentHint is called again; any other tool fails with MCP_CLIENT_TOOL_CALL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is not resent.

hostAllowlist.notes: allowedHosts on a url entry limits the connect, every POST, OAuth requests routed through the transport fetch and every redirect hop to listed hosts. With the default fetch a disallowed hop is blocked before it is sent; with a custom fetch it is checked from the response URL afterwards.

traceContextPropagation.notes: Each request's _meta carries W3C traceparent, tracestate and baggage, taken from the entry's traceContext provider or from the span making the request.

cachedToolDefinitions.notes: listToolDefinitions() returns the tools/list entries as plain JSON with the server name, version and instructions. toolsFromDefinitions() rebuilds executable tools from it without connecting; each connects on its first call.

listChanged.notes: No stream is opened. The server pushes the notification unprompted and the handler the application registered runs.

resources.notes: The list and read calls are the same.

subscribe.notes: resources/subscribe is never sent. subscribeResource() needs the subscriptions/listen stream and throws an error naming the negotiated revision.

logging.notes: logging/setLevel is never sent, so the server decides the level. The notifications/message handler is registered all the same, and the logLevel _meta key is still attached to each request.

evidence.note: After initialize the client sent notifications/initialized, tools/list and tools/call, each with _meta {"io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel":"info"}, and no logging/setLevel (wire.jsonl).

tasks.notes: Only the SEP-2663 extension form is implemented: a result with resultType task. The 2025-11-25 task-augmented request form is not sent.

The lockfile also holds client and core 2.3.1, for the published @mastra/mcp 1.18.0 used in compatibility tests and as the peer of ext-apps 2.0.4, and @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.32.1 and 1.32.2 for packages/mcp-registry-registry, packages/playground-ui and third-party SDKs. None of those is the MCP client. Unpatched: patchedDependencies in pnpm-workspace.yaml lists nine packages and patches/ holds twelve files, none for an @modelcontextprotocol package. The workspace overrides raise older @modelcontextprotocol ranges to fixed releases and do not reach 2.4.0. @mastra/mcp is its own package: @mastra/core depends on @modelcontextprotocol/server for types and not on the client. The SDK's default negotiation mode is legacy and Mastra passes auto, so leading with server/discover is Mastra's choice, and 2026-07-28 is named in Mastra's own source as the pin value. The fallback handshake offers the SDK's LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION, 2025-11-25, and accepts back to 2024-10-07, a revision this registry does not track. pinsProtocolVersion is left unset for that reason.

fx.title: fx (native engine)
fx.description: Coding agent CLI from Vercel Labs, one native Zig binary. Its MCP client is hand-written in Zig with no SDK, and one engine serves the terminal app, `fx ask` and ACP editors. It sends `server/discover` at 2026-07-28 first and falls back to the `initialize` handshake. It consumes tools and elicitation. Resources, prompts and HTTP+SSE were removed in 0.0.15.

stdio.notes: One process per server in its own process group, one JSON-RPC message per line. The child gets HOME, LOGNAME, PATH, SHELL, TERM and USER from fx plus the entry's env, and nothing else of fx's environment. stderr lines go to the debug log. Each new process is probed again.

sse.notes: An entry with "type": "sse" is parsed and then held back with "HTTP+SSE servers are not supported". The changelog lists the removal under 0.0.15.

streamableHttp.notes: POST with a JSON or SSE answer. On a 2026-07-28 server every request carries MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method and, for a call, Mcp-Name. A broken stream is re-issued with a new id and a cancel closes the stream. Redirects are not followed. The 2025 session behaviour is under byProtocolVersion.

oauth.notes: Discovery reads the WWW-Authenticate challenge, then RFC 9728 resource metadata, then authorization server metadata with OpenID Connect discovery as a fallback. The server must list S256. Registration tries a configured oauth.client_id, then a client ID metadata document when the server supports them and the entry sets oauth.client_metadata_url, then Dynamic Client Registration as a native public client named fx. fx hosts no metadata document, so a default install registers dynamically and clientIdMetadataDocument is recorded false. The redirect is a loopback listener on 127.0.0.1. A 403 insufficient_scope challenge starts a step-up sign-in. A missing iss is refused when the server advertised it. Sign-out revokes the token.

evidence.note: Options, register and authorize. The client_metadata_url comment reads "None until fx hosts one."
Resource metadata and authorization server metadata URLs, and the S256 requirement.
Authorization URL with resource, the state and iss check, the registration body, and the token request.
iss by RFC 9207.
Loopback redirect.

header.notes: headers, header_env and bearer_token_env on an HTTP entry. An entry that names an unset variable, or a value a header cannot carry, is held back with the reason.

tools.notes: tools/list follows nextCursor for up to 100 pages and restarts once on an invalid cursor. A tool with no name, an inputSchema that is not an object, a repeated name or, over HTTP, an invalid x-mcp-header annotation is dropped and counted. MCP tools are not in the model's tool list: the model finds, opens and runs them through the toolbox tool, under the name mcp_<server>_<tool>. A server an ACP editor supplies is sent every turn unless the editor sets _meta.fx.alwaysLoaded to false.

listChanged.notes: On 2026-07-28 fx opens subscriptions/listen asking for toolsListChanged only. On a 2025 server it takes notifications/tools/list_changed. Either marks the list stale and it is listed again at the next need. A positive ttlMs on a 2026 list also expires it.

result.notes: The whole result goes to the model as one JSON string inside an envelope: {"server", "tool", "result": {content, structuredContent, isError}}. Nothing compares the two fields. An envelope over 16 KiB is stored, and the model gets a 4 KiB preview with a handle for read_tool_result. The files the note reads did not change between its pin and c3dc80c4, apart from one HTTP connection fix in src/mcp (29b9c67f).

evidence.note: The read tier for tool result handling lives in that repo (AGENTS.md); this entry summarises its note, which read the fx source at 3fd4905.

content.notes: Text blocks stay as block objects in the envelope, with their annotations and _meta. A result with no content key, or a content that is not an array, is invalid and the model gets a failure text. An empty array is sent as "content":[] with no placeholder.

structuredContent.notes: A JSON value in the envelope next to content, unvalidated, non-object values included. In a stored result's 4 KiB preview content comes first, so a text mirror longer than that leaves no structuredContent in the preview.

outputSchema.notes: Stored and hashed into the tool's definition digest, never checked against structuredContent. A tool whose outputSchema is not an object, or names a dialect other than 2020-12 or draft-07, is left out of the catalog.

audience.notes: Checked for shape only. A block addressed to the user still reaches the model with the annotation visible in the envelope. A malformed audience fails the whole result.

isError.notes: The same envelope, structuredContent included, returned as a tool failure.

media.notes: Image blocks and image/ embedded blobs (png, jpeg, gif, webp) reach a vision model as image parts. Audio and other binary blocks keep their block with the data removed and a delivery note. resource_link blocks and embedded text resources stay in the envelope as JSON.

_meta.notes: Result-level _meta is dropped where the answer is read. Block-level _meta stays in the envelope text. Tool-level _meta is only hashed, so _meta.ui.visibility has no effect.

resources.notes: The engine sends five kinds of request: server/discover, initialize, tools/list, tools/call and subscriptions/listen. The changelog lists the removal of resources and the resource command under 0.0.15.

listChanged.notes: The listen filter asks for toolsListChanged only, and a resources/list_changed notice has nothing to refresh.

subscribe.notes: No resources/subscribe request, and the listen filter never names resourceSubscriptions.

prompts.notes: No prompts/list or prompts/get request. Removed with resources in 0.0.15.

listChanged.notes: The listen filter asks for toolsListChanged only.

completions.notes: No completion/complete request.

sampling.notes: Never declared. A 2026 input_required round that asks for sampling ends the call as unsupported input. A 2025 sampling/createMessage request gets -32601.

evidence.note: The host names sampling and roots as unsupported methods.

elicitation.notes: Declared per surface. The terminal app declares form and url. fx ask declares both only when the output mode is a terminal and stdin and stderr are TTYs, and nothing otherwise. An ACP session declares the modes the editor declared and forwards the questions to it. On 2026-07-28 the questions arrive as input_required rounds on tools/call, on 2025 as elicitation/create requests.

form.notes: A flat object of string, number, integer, boolean, single-select and multi-select properties, at most 32. The answer is checked against the schema before it is sent. A form the client cannot read gets -32602 on 2025 and ends the call as malformed on 2026.

url.notes: Only HTTPS URLs, or HTTP to a loopback host. fx asks before opening the link and flags a Punycode or non-ASCII host. On 2025 it waits for notifications/elicitation/complete and handles the -32042 error that lists required URL elicitations.

evidence.note: The terminal app.
fx ask.
ACP sessions.
Reading the editor's declared modes.

roots.notes: Never declared. A 2026 round that asks for roots ends the call as unsupported input, and a 2025 roots/list request gets -32601.

listChanged.notes: Nothing sends notifications/roots/list_changed.

logging.notes: No logging/setLevel, and the per-request _meta carries no logLevel key. The notification handler has no branch for notifications/message, so one is dropped. A stdio server's stderr goes to the debug log, which is a separate channel.

instructions.notes: Kept from the last discover or initialize result. They reach the model with a tool's schema when the toolbox opens or runs that server's tool, cut at the mcp_server_instructions_bytes limit. They are not in the system prompt.

icons.notes: A tool's icons are validated, stored and hashed into the definition digest. Nothing renders them.

tasks.notes: No tasks request. A result whose resultType is anything but complete or input_required, "task" included, is read as unrecognized and treated as invalid.

jsonSchema.notes: A tool schema that names any other $schema is rejected and the tool is left out. Elicitation forms accept only a flat object of primitive properties. How much of a tool's inputSchema is checked before a call was not read.

io.modelcontextprotocol/ui.notes: The declared capability object holds elicitation or nothing. No file under src/ names ui:// or resourceUri, and a tool marked app-only stays available to the model.

modelInitiatedResourceRead.notes: fx reads no resources at all.

deferredToolLoading.notes: MCP servers are listed in a toolbox menu and their tools stay out of the tool list, so every request sends the same tools. The toolbox tool searches, opens and runs them. The probe ran 0.0.16, where capability_search and mcp_select_tool did this job.

lazyServerStart.notes: Each server starts when something first needs its tool list or calls it, and is kept until a reload drops it.

standardRequestHeaders.notes: On 2026-07-28 over HTTP: Mcp-Method on every request, Mcp-Name on tools/call, and Mcp-Param-* headers from a tool's x-mcp-header annotations. A tool with an invalid annotation is dropped from the list.

cacheableResult.notes: A 2026 tool list is served from cache only while every page's ttlMs holds, capped at 24 hours. A 2025 list stays fresh until it is invalidated or the process restarts.

pi.title: pi
pi.description: TypeScript coding agent CLI from Earendil Works, formerly badlogic/pi-mono. Its README said "No MCP" until September 2026. Since 0.99.0 it ships its own hand-written MCP client, @earendil-works/pi-mcp, as a built-in extension that is on by default and loads when a server is configured. By default MCP tools are not declared to the model: scripts the model writes for the codemode tool call them.

stdio.notes: A command entry is spawned through cross-spawn with the parent environment plus the entry's env, in its own process group on POSIX. env values may reference ${NAME} or run a command with !cmd. stderr is piped, and its last 2000 characters are shown when a connect fails or the connection drops. Close ends stdin, sends SIGTERM to the group after 500 ms and SIGKILL 2 s later; on Windows it runs taskkill /T /F. A dropped connection reconnects on the next call.

sse.notes: An entry with type sse is rejected when the config is validated, with a message that points at the Streamable HTTP URL. A url entry always uses Streamable HTTP, and there is no fallback to HTTP+SSE. The pi-mcp README lists legacy HTTP+SSE as outside the initial core.

streamableHttp.notes: The only remote transport. A response may be JSON or SSE. After notifications/initialized the client opens the GET stream and treats 405 as no stream. A dropped GET stream, or a response stream that carried event ids, is resumed with Last-Event-ID under exponential backoff, five attempts by default. MCP-Protocol-Version carries the negotiated version on every request after initialize, and Mcp-Session-Id is echoed. Close sends DELETE with a one second limit. A connect is retried twice after a network error or a 408, 429 or 5xx other than 501.

oauth.notes: Applies to a url server with no Authorization header and no auth block. A connection never opens a browser: it sends the stored access token, refreshes it 30 s before expiry or after a 401, and otherwise marks the server as needing sign-in until the user runs /mcp or pi mcp login. A 403 with insufficient_scope also asks for sign-in, with the challenged scopes added to the granted ones. Without a clientId pi offers its Client ID Metadata Document on pi.dev when the authorization server advertises client_id_metadata_document_supported and the none token auth method, and registers dynamically otherwise. The callback is a loopback server on 127.0.0.1, or a redirect URL the user pastes. Tokens are stored in mcp-auth.json in the agent directory, keyed by server name and URL, and refreshes are serialized across pi processes with a lock file. The flow code is adapted from typescript-sdk v1.29.0 src/client/auth.ts.

An auth block with a provider name sends the current token of that pi /login provider as the bearer token; it is refused in project mcp.json files and needs https or a loopback host.

tools.notes: tools/list is called only when the server declares the tools capability. Every page is followed, with a duplicate-cursor guard and a cap of 1000 pages. Tools are registered as mcp__<server>__<tool>, with characters outside letters, digits and _ replaced by _ and a hash suffix past 64 characters or on a collision. The default exposure is codemode, so the model gets no declaration for an MCP tool. tools/call carries a progress token, a progress notification resets the per-request timeout of 60 s, and an abort or timeout sends notifications/cancelled. The four annotation hints are passed to permission extensions.

listChanged.notes: A listener added after connect calls tools/list again. New tools are registered. Tools the server dropped are re-registered as hidden, because pi cannot unregister a tool. The listener is added whether or not the server declared tools.listChanged.

result.notes: On the default codemode route the model never receives the result: a script gets the whole CallToolResult without _meta, uncut, and only what the script returns reaches the model. With exposure direct, or deferred once tool_search has loaded the tool, content reaches the model and structuredContent fills in only when content is empty.

evidence.note: The read tier for tool result handling lives in that repo (AGENTS.md); this entry summarises its note, which read the pi source at 8636e21.

content.notes: On the direct and deferred routes text and image blocks reach the model. Text past 20 KB is cut in the middle and the full text is saved to a temp file named in the result. An empty content array with no structuredContent sends nothing from the adapter, and the provider layer supplies its own placeholder.

structuredContent.notes: Reaches the model only when content is empty or absent, as one text block of pretty-printed JSON. Codemode scripts always receive it.

outputSchema.notes: structuredContent is never validated against outputSchema. The schema is wrapped into the result type that codemode declarations show to scripts.

audience.notes: annotations.audience is in the types and nothing reads it. A block addressed to the user reaches the model like any other.

isError.notes: The content text carries the error. An isError result with no text gets the line "MCP tool <server>/<tool> returned an error". In a codemode script an isError result resolves and does not throw.

media.notes: Images pass through as images. Audio becomes a text line saying it was omitted. A resource_link becomes a text line that names read_mcp_resource. Embedded text resources become text, and other blobs are saved to a temp file. A content array holding only non-text blocks counts as non-empty, so structuredContent is not used for it.

modelInitiatedResourceRead.notes: The same three tool names as Codex and opencode, on purpose: the source says models trained on those tools use them unchanged. The tools take the widest exposure among the servers with resources, so on a default install a codemode script calls them and the model has no declaration for them. A resource_link block in a tool result names read_mcp_resource and the server.

codeModeToolExposure.notes: The default exposure. An MCP tool is callable as tools.mcp__<server>__<tool>() from JavaScript the model writes for the codemode tool. Scripts find tools with searchTools(), describeTool(), describeNamespace() and ALL_TOOLS. The codemode tool is activated when an enabled server has codemode tools, unless autoEnableCodemode is false. Other exposures are deferred, direct and hidden, set per server or per tool.

deferredToolLoading.notes: Opt-in with exposure deferred on a server or a tool. The tools are not declared until the tool_search tool, a BM25 ranker over tool and namespace text, loads matches for the next model call. Loaded tools are then called directly. The default route is codemode, not this one.

sessionRecovery.notes: A 404 on a request that carried a session id raises McpSessionExpiredError. The connection opens a new session and retries the request once, tool calls included, on the reasoning that the server did not run it. Listing and reading resources are also retried once after a 408, 429 or 5xx; tool calls are not.

projectConfigTrustGate.notes: The project file .pi/mcp.json is read only after the project is trusted. A project entry without command, url or type may override enabled, exposure and toolExposure of a global server and nothing else. A project entry cannot use auth.provider.

replaceableBuiltInClient.notes: MCP is a built-in extension marked replaceable. An installed extension that registers /mcp takes over and the built-in one does not load. --no-mcp turns it off for one run, and -builtin:mcp in the extensions setting turns it off for good. Extensions add servers for a session with pi.registerMcpServer(). SDK sessions do not load built-in extensions.

conformanceSuiteInCi.notes: CI runs the client scenarios of @modelcontextprotocol/conformance 0.2.0-alpha.11 against pi's HTTP connection and sign-in code at three revisions and compares every check with a committed baseline.

crewai.title: crewAI
crewai.description: Python framework for crews of role-playing agents and for flows. An agent takes MCP servers through mcps=[...]. crewAI serves that with its own MCPClient on the official mcp SDK and opens a new session for every tool call. crewai-tools adds a second route, MCPServerAdapter, on the third-party mcpadapt package. Only tools are consumed. Every route declares no client capabilities and sends the SDK placeholder name mcp.

speaksMcpVia.notes: On the native mcps route crewai.mcp.MCPClient is a thin wrapper that owns one SDK ClientSession, so the SDK is the MCP client and decides the handshake, the revision and the client name. The crewai-tools route, MCPServerAdapter, goes through the third-party adapter mcpadapt (0.1.19 or 0.1.20 by Python version), which builds its own ClientSession on the same SDK.

stdio.notes: MCPServerStdio(command, args, env) runs the SDK's stdio_client. The child environment is the SDK's default inherited variables plus the config's env, passed through an optional module-level _env_filter_hook. There is no cwd setting. adk-python.title: Google ADK (Python)
adk-python.description: Google's Agent Development Kit for Python. An LlmAgent reaches MCP servers through McpToolset, ADK's own session pool and tool wrapper over the official Python SDK's ClientSession. A default construction sends clientInfo google-adk, declares no client capabilities and runs the initialize handshake at 2025-11-25. The SDK is an optional extra that admits 1.x and 2.x, and 2026-07-28 needs SDK 2.x plus the default-off ADK_ENABLE_MCP_MODERN_PROTOCOL switch.

stdio.notes: StdioConnectionParams wraps the SDK's StdioServerParameters and goes to stdio_client with an errlog stream that defaults to sys.stderr. One session is pooled per toolset. The timeout field defaults to 5 seconds, bounds connect plus initialize, and is also the ClientSession read timeout for every stdio request. An agent config file cannot declare a stdio server unless ADK_ALLOW_CONFIG_STDIO_MCP_SERVERS is set.

from_config rejects stdio params unless the environment variable or the in-process override allows them.

sse.notes: Chosen by passing SseConnectionParams. ADK does not detect the transport from a URL and does not fall back from one HTTP transport to the other. Headers, a 5 second timeout and a 300 second read timeout go to the SDK's sse_client.

streamableHttp.notes: Chosen by passing StreamableHTTPConnectionParams. ADK builds the HTTP client itself, with the merged headers and a 5 second timeout with a 300 second read timeout, and hands it to the SDK's streamable_http_client. terminate_on_close defaults to true. Sessions are pooled per merged header set and closed after 900 seconds idle. ADK sets no MCP-Protocol-Version header of its own. The Agent Registry and API Registry integrations build this transport.

evidence.note: _StreamableHttpClientWrapper passes the pre-built client to streamable_http_client.

oauth.notes: The flow is ADK's generic tool-auth framework, and the SDK's OAuth client is not used. The application passes an auth_scheme and an auth_credential with a registered client id. ADK builds the authorization URL, hands it to the application in an adk_request_credential function call, exchanges the code, refreshes the token and sends it as a Bearer header. Nothing reads a 401 challenge. Protected resource metadata discovery is defined and has no caller under src. Authorization server metadata is fetched only for an ExtendedOAuth2 scheme that carries an issuer_url. There is no dynamic registration, no client ID metadata document and no resource parameter. PKCE S256 is used when the credential has no client secret or asks for it.

The credential request function call is named adk_request_credential.

header.notes: Static headers on the connection params, a header_provider callback evaluated per request context, and headers derived from an auth_credential: Bearer, Basic, other HTTP schemes and header API keys. Auth headers win over header_provider on a name collision. ADK adds its own User-Agent and x-goog-api-client tokens. When google-auth would use a client certificate, the HTTP transport switches to mTLS and attaches Application Default Credentials as a Bearer token for https googleapis.com hosts only.

tools.notes: One tools/list request per listing with no cursor, so a second page is never fetched. The list is fetched once per invocation unless tool_list_cache_ttl_seconds is set. tool_filter and tool_name_prefix select and rename tools. A tool whose name matches one of five reserved ADK function names is skipped. Tools are sorted by name. Each description and each schema description is wrapped in untrusted-content markers before it reaches the model. ADK passes an application progress_callback to call_tool and passes none by default.

What the model receives then depends on the model backend. The default Gemini backend sends the dict as built. AnthropicLlm sends the content text when content is non-empty.

agent-framework.title: Microsoft Agent Framework
agent-framework.description: Microsoft's agent framework, one repository with a Python binding and a .NET binding. The Python binding has its own MCP client class, MCPTool, built on the Python SDK's Client, and the capability rows describe it. The .NET binding has no client class: the application builds an McpClient with the C# SDK and the framework wraps its tools. Notes on each row say where .NET differs.

stdio.notes: MCPStdioTool passes command, args, env and encoding to the SDK's stdio_client. Extra keyword arguments go into StdioServerParameters. .NET: the framework builds no stdio client. An application passes its own McpClient, on any transport the C# SDK offers.

sse.notes: The Python binding has no SSE transport class. The exported MCP tool classes are MCPStdioTool, MCPStreamableHTTPTool and the MCPWebsocketTool stub, and streamable_http_client is the only HTTP transport imported. .NET: both clients the framework builds set HttpTransportMode.StreamableHttp, with a comment that this stops the client negotiating down to HTTP+SSE. An application-built McpClient gets the C# SDK default, AutoDetect.

evidence.note: The MCP tool classes the package exports.
The only HTTP transport import.
.NET declarative handler pins Streamable HTTP.
.NET Foundry toolbox pins Streamable HTTP.
ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0 (tag v2.2.0). TransportMode defaults to AutoDetect.

streamableHttp.notes: MCPStreamableHTTPTool calls the SDK's streamable_http_client, with terminate_on_close defaulting to true. The httpx2 client the framework makes follows redirects, uses a 30 second timeout with a 300 second read timeout, and stores no response cookies. An application can pass its own httpx2.AsyncClient. .NET: DefaultMcpToolHandler builds one Streamable HTTP client per invocation and FoundryToolboxService one per response, both with the standalone GET stream off.

evidence.note: The two timeout constants.

websocket.notes: MCPWebsocketTool is still exported and marked deprecated. Its get_mcp_client raises RuntimeError, so it cannot connect.

oauth.notes: MCPStreamableHTTPTool has no auth parameter, and no file under python/packages imports mcp.client.auth. An application can pass its own httpx2.AsyncClient through http_client and attach the SDK's OAuth provider to it. The framework does not set that up. FoundryToolbox authenticates with a bearer token from an Azure credential. .NET: neither client the framework builds sets HttpClientTransportOptions.OAuth. The Agent_MCP_Server_Auth sample sets it on a transport the application builds, which is the C# SDK's feature.

http_client is the only route to custom HTTP auth.

header.notes: static_headers and header_provider add headers to requests whose origin matches the configured url, and remove them when a redirect leaves that origin. header_provider receives the run's keyword arguments. The header set used to connect is bound to the session, and a run with a different set reconnects first. .NET: DefaultMcpToolHandler passes the workflow's headers as AdditionalHeaders and rejects a Host header.

tools.notes: tools/list is called only when the server declares the tools capability. Pages are followed by cursor up to 100 pages and 1,000 tools, and discovery fails past either limit. On 2026-07-28 the SDK's response cache honours ttlMs and cacheScope. A tool whose execution.taskSupport is required is skipped with a warning. Names are normalised to A-Za-z0-9_.- with an optional tool_name_prefix, and no server prefix by default. An object inputSchema without properties gets an empty one. Call arguments are filtered to the properties the schema declares. approval_mode defaults to None, so calls run without approval. Tool _meta from tools/list is sent back as request _meta on tools/call.

listChanged.notes: On 2026-07-28 the framework opens Client.listen for tools and prompts when the server capability sets listChanged, and reloads the catalog on each event. A lost subscription is reopened with backoff from 0.1 to 2 seconds after a full reload. On the handshake path notifications/tools/list_changed schedules the same reload. A reload keeps the existing FunctionTool for a tool whose remote name is unchanged, so a changed description or inputSchema does not reach the model. A caller-owned Client on a handshake-era server gets no automatic refresh. .NET: no list-changed handling in dotnet/src.

evidence.note: Subscription loop and recovery.

A retained tool is not rebuilt on reload.

result.notes: tool_result_content defaults to structured_first: when structuredContent is present, one JSON text block replaces every content block. The other modes are content_first, content_only, structured_only and both, set per MCPTool, and parse_tool_results replaces the parser. .NET differs: the C# SDK's McpClientTool returns native content only when the result has no isError, no structuredContent and no application _meta, and otherwise the whole CallToolResult as JSON.

content.notes: Under the default mode content reaches the model only when structuredContent is absent. content_first, content_only and both keep it. .NET: native content when nothing else is present, otherwise inside the JSON envelope.

The security middleware reads _meta.ifc for integrity and confidentiality labels. .NET: any application _meta key switches the result to the JSON envelope, which includes it.

vscode.title: Visual Studio Code
vscode.description: Microsoft's editor. Its MCP client is hand-written in the workbench, with no MCP SDK, and serves Copilot Chat, which is vendored in the same repo at extensions/copilot and has no MCP client of its own. It declares roots, sampling, elicitation (form and url), tasks and the MCP Apps extension on every connection, and sends 2025-11-25 in initialize. stdio.notes: Spawned from the Node extension host with envFile and env merged over process.env. stdout is split on newlines. stderr lines go to the server's output log as warnings. Not available in the web build, which registers only the common HTTP service.

sse.notes: Fallback when the first POST to the URL returns a 4xx other than 401 or 403, or when a POST response carries an SSE endpoint event. The legacy SSE stream then holds the session.

streamableHttp.notes: Tried first for every HTTP server. Handles Mcp-Session-Id, the GET backchannel with Last-Event-ID, DELETE on close, and a 400 or 404 on a session id as a reason to re-initialize. Requests do not carry the MCP-Protocol-Version header that 2025-06-18 and later require after initialize. Only the OAuth metadata fetches send it.

oauth.notes: On a 401 or 403 the client reads resource_metadata from WWW-Authenticate, falls back to the well-known protected resource paths, then to authorization server metadata, then to default endpoints derived from the URL. A stored client id wins. Without one, CIMD is used when the server advertises client_id_metadata_document_supported and the product sets authClientIdMetadataUrl; the Code - OSS product.json does not set it, and the Microsoft builds' product.json is not in the repo. Otherwise DCR, and if DCR fails the user is prompted for a client id and secret. The DCR request lists device_code among its grant types, and no device flow was found in the dynamic provider. Enterprise-managed servers can use cross-app access through a configured IdP.

header.notes: Configured headers go on every POST, GET and DELETE. A server definition can also name an authentication provider id and scopes, whose token becomes the Authorization header. Configured headers and credentials are stripped on a cross-origin redirect.

tools.notes: Hugging Face traffic includes tool calls from this client. tools/list is called only when the server declares tools, and follows nextCursor with no duplicate-cursor guard. Each inputSchema is validated against the draft-07 meta-schema and a tool that fails is dropped with a warning. Tool lists are cached so tools show before a server starts. Calls carry progressToken, vscode.conversationId, vscode.requestId and W3C trace context in _meta.

langflow.title: Langflow
langflow.description: Visual builder for AI flows and agents, served as a web app and a desktop app. Its MCP Tools component connects to MCP servers registered under Settings > MCP Servers and hands their tools to an agent or runs one tool directly. The client is Langflow's own wrapper on the official mcp SDK in lfx.base.mcp.util. langchain-mcp-adapters is declared as an extra and never imported. Only tools are consumed, no client capability is declared, and the wire name is the SDK placeholder mcp. Langflow also serves flows as an MCP server, which this entry does not cover.

stdio.notes: A server config with a command runs through the SDK's stdio_client. The child gets the SDK's default inherited variables plus DEBUG=true, PATH and the config's env. Headers on a stdio config are inserted into argv as --headers key value, for mcp-proxy. mcp-use.title: mcp-use
mcp-use.description: Open source MCP framework from mcp-use, Inc. with a TypeScript binding and a Python binding in one repository. The client side is @mcp-use/client (MCPClient, connectors, OAuth, React hooks) and @mcp-use/agent (MCPAgent, a provider-neutral tool loop) in TypeScript, and the mcp-use PyPI package (MCPClient and a LangChain MCPAgent) in Python. The repository also holds an MCP server framework (the mcp-use npm package), an inspector, a CLI, a scaffolder, a tunnel and an MCP Apps view SDK, which are out of scope here. The rows describe a default MCPClient and MCPAgent construction of the TypeScript binding, which the root README presents as the framework and which runs on the v2 SDK. Row notes say where the Python binding differs. Both bindings send anonymized telemetry to PostHog by default.

The child gets the SDK's safe default environment plus env, and stderr is piped to errlog by default. oauth.notes: On by default. MCPClient attaches an OAuth provider to every HTTP server whose entry has no authProvider, no authToken and no Authorization header, unless oauth is false. A connect or later request that needs authorization runs the flow and retries once. The Node provider listens on 127.0.0.1:33418 (walking up 10 ports, then an ephemeral port), opens the browser, and persists client registrations and tokens under ~/.mcp-use/oauth with mode 0600. Client metadata is a public client with authorization_code and refresh_token grants. DCR, PKCE, RFC 9728 discovery, the resource parameter and the RFC 9207 iss check run in the SDK. A Client ID Metadata Document is used only when the clientMetadataUrl option is set. After an anonymous connection, RFC 9728 metadata is probed for 2 seconds to mark mixed-auth servers. The browser entry uses a popup or redirect. Python: the default auth {} also builds an OAuth helper, written by mcp-use on authlib, with a callback on localhost:8080, DCR, PKCE S256, CIMD when client_metadata_url is set and tokens under ~/.mcp_use/tokens. A server with no discoverable OAuth metadata connects without auth.

zed.title: Zed
zed.description: Code editor with a built-in agent. Zed calls MCP servers context servers and speaks MCP through its own hand-written JSON-RPC client in the context_server crate, with no MCP SDK. The client declares no capabilities, uses tools and prompts, and does not use resources. External ACP agents run in Zed receive the configured servers and connect to them with their own MCP clients.

stdio.notes: Launched through the system shell with piped stdin, stdout and stderr; stderr goes to the log. A server marked remote: true in a remote project is launched on the remote host through Zed's remote stdio launcher. Extensions can supply the command.

sse.notes: A url server always uses the Streamable HTTP transport. There is no legacy HTTP+SSE transport and no fallback to one.

streamableHttp.notes: POSTs each message with Accept for JSON and event-stream and reads either kind of response. Keeps Mcp-Session-Id and sends DELETE on drop. Sends MCP-Protocol-Version only after negotiating 2025-06-18 or 2025-11-25. Never opens the GET stream, so server messages arrive only on the SSE response to a POST. A 404 for an expired session is reported as an error with no re-initialize.

oauth.notes: Starts on a 401 at initialize or later, unless a static Authorization header is configured. Discovers protected resource metadata, then authorization server metadata by RFC 8414 and OIDC URLs, and requires S256 PKCE. Uses CIMD (https://zed.dev/oauth/client-metadata.json) when the server advertises it, DCR otherwise, or a pre-registered client_id and secret from settings. Sends resource on the authorization, token and refresh requests. The callback is a loopback server, the session is stored in the system keychain, and a 401 triggers one refresh and retry. The callback's iss parameter is not checked.

header.notes: A headers map on a url server is sent on every POST and on the DELETE. With an Authorization header set, Zed does not start OAuth.

none.notes: A url server with no headers and no stored session connects without credentials until it returns 401.

tools.notes: tools/list is called only when the server declares tools, once at start and again on list_changed. It is sent with no cursor and nextCursor is never read, so only the first page is used. Each call is authorized through authorize_third_party_tool, which follows the agent's tool permission settings. Tool calls time out after context_server_timeout or the per-server timeout, capped at 600 seconds.

listChanged.notes: The only server notification Zed subscribes to. It re-lists the server's tools. Registered only when the server declares tools.

result.notes: Text and image blocks from content reach the model. structuredContent, outputSchema, annotations and _meta are parsed or ignored and never read. A result with no content key fails deserialization.

evidence.note: The read tier for tool result handling lives in that repo (AGENTS.md); this entry summarises its note, which read the Zed source at 0cfc4a4 (Zed 1.30.0).
The tools/call loop the note describes was checked at this commit and matches it.

structuredContent.notes: Kept on the parsed response and never read.

outputSchema.notes: Stored with the tool and never read. No validation.

isError.notes: The concatenated text blocks of content become the error message.

media.notes: Images reach the model as image parts when the model supports images. Audio, resource and resource_link blocks are logged and dropped.

resources.notes: The types define resources/list, resources/read and subscribe, and no client code sends them. Resource capabilities on the server are not checked anywhere.

listChanged.notes: No handler for notifications/resources/list_changed.

subscribe.notes: No resources/subscribe call and no resources/updated handler.

prompts.notes: Each prompt becomes a slash command in the agent panel, prefixed with the server id when its name clashes. Prompts with more than one argument are skipped. A prompt with one argument takes it as free text. prompts/get messages are added to the thread as user and assistant content, with annotations kept.

elicitation.notes: ClientCapabilities has no elicitation field. The elicitation handling in agent_servers belongs to ACP.

logging.notes: No handler for notifications/message and no logging/setLevel call. Server stderr goes to Zed's log.

ts-sdk-client.title: TypeScript SDK Client
ts-sdk-client.description: The Client class of the official TypeScript SDK, published as @modelcontextprotocol/client. Rows describe what new Client(clientInfo) with no options declares and does, at 2.4.0 (the version the probe pins and Mastra resolves) and at the clone HEAD, which is 8 commits past the 2.4.0 tag. A default construction runs the 2025 initialize handshake at 2025-11-25 and declares no capabilities. server/discover and 2026-07-28 are reached only with versionNegotiation set to auto or a pin.

stdio.notes: StdioClientTransport, exported from the @modelcontextprotocol/client/stdio subpath. Spawns without a shell. The child gets a whitelist of environment variables (PATH, HOME and similar; on Windows APPDATA, PATH, SYSTEMROOT, USERPROFILE and others) plus the env the application passes. stderr is inherited unless the application sets it. In auto mode the server/discover probe runs on a second short-lived process spawned from the same parameters.

sse.notes: SSEClientTransport is exported and marked deprecated in favour of Streamable HTTP. The SDK does not fall back from one to the other. The class comment shows the application doing the fallback itself. Redirects are followed only within the request origin unless redirectPolicy is follow.

streamableHttp.notes: StreamableHTTPClientTransport. Sends mcp-protocol-version after the handshake. Reconnects a dropped SSE stream up to 2 times with backoff from 1 s to 30 s. Same-origin redirect policy by default. On a 2026-07-28 request the protocol header and Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name are derived from the request body, so the header cannot disagree with the body era.

oauth.notes: Off until the application passes an OAuthClientProvider as the transport authProvider. Then the auth() flow discovers protected resource metadata, then authorization server metadata through RFC 8414 and OpenID Connect paths. It uses a CIMD URL as the client_id when the provider sets clientMetadataUrl and the server advertises client_id_metadata_document_supported, and registers dynamically otherwise. PKCE is S256. The resource parameter goes on the authorize and token requests. The RFC 9207 iss parameter is checked. A 403 insufficient_scope triggers one step-up reauthorization by default. ClientCredentialsProvider and PrivateKeyJwtProvider cover client_credentials. 2.4.0 always adds prompt=consent when the scope includes offline_access; HEAD adds skipOfflineAccessConsentPrompt.

header.notes: requestInit.headers on either HTTP transport are sent on every request. Authorization, mcp-session-id and mcp-protocol-version set by the transport take precedence, so a static Authorization header is sent only while an authProvider has no token. An AuthProvider of the form { token: async () => key } sends a bearer token without OAuth.

tools.notes: listTools() with no cursor walks every page, up to listMaxPages (64), stops on a page that repeats the one before, and caches the aggregate. Passing a cursor fetches one page. Against a server with no tools capability it returns an empty list without a request unless enforceStrictCapabilities is set. callTool() validates structuredContent against the outputSchema of a tool it has seen in a cached tools/list, and throws when a tool with an outputSchema returns no structuredContent. With a cold cache it validates nothing.

listChanged.notes: A notifications/tools/list_changed always evicts the cached tools/list. The application is told only when it passes ClientOptions.listChanged.tools, which by default refetches the list and calls onChanged, optionally debounced. The handler is registered only when the server advertises tools.listChanged.

evidence.note: Output-schema validation reads the cached tools/list entry.

resources.notes: listResources(), listResourceTemplates() and readResource() are on the Client, with the same paging and cache rules as tools. resources/read results are cached per URI and evicted on notifications/resources/updated.

listChanged.notes: Same as tools: the cache entry is always evicted, and the application hears of it through ClientOptions.listChanged.resources.

subscribe.notes: subscribeResource() and unsubscribeResource() send resources/subscribe on a 2025 connection. The application registers its own handler for notifications/resources/updated; the client only evicts its cached read.

prompts.notes: listPrompts() and getPrompt() are on the Client. Paging and the missing-capability rule match tools.

listChanged.notes: Through ClientOptions.listChanged.prompts.

completions.notes: complete() sends completion/complete for a prompt or resource template argument. The SDK has no UI that calls it.

sampling.notes: Not declared by default. The application passes capabilities.sampling and registers setRequestHandler('sampling/createMessage'). The SDK validates the request and the handler result against the negotiated era, including the tool-use result shape when the request carries tools. The class comment marks sampling deprecated as of 2026-07-28 (SEP-2577).

context.notes: includeContext reaches the application handler unchanged. Honouring it is the handler's job.

tools.notes: A request with tools or toolChoice is validated against the tool-use result schema.

evidence.note: The constructor copies options.capabilities, or {} when none are given.
assertRequestHandlerCapability: registering a sampling, elicitation or roots handler throws unless the matching capability was declared.

elicitation.notes: Not declared by default. The application passes capabilities.elicitation and registers setRequestHandler('elicitation/create'). The SDK rejects a request in a mode the client did not declare, validates the result, and fills schema defaults into an accepted form when elicitation.form.applyDefaults is set. An empty elicitation object means form only.

url.notes: Declared as elicitation.url. A URL-mode request is rejected when only form was declared.

roots.notes: Not declared by default. The application passes capabilities.roots and registers setRequestHandler('roots/list'). Marked deprecated as of 2026-07-28 (SEP-2577).

listChanged.notes: Sending notifications/roots/list_changed throws unless capabilities.roots.listChanged was declared.

logging.notes: No notifications/message handler is registered by default, and the Protocol layer drops a notification with no handler. The application registers one with setNotificationHandler and may call setLoggingLevel(), which is marked deprecated as of 2026-07-28. The logger option added after 2.4.0 is for the SDK's own diagnostics.

instructions.notes: Kept from the initialize result or the discover result and returned by getInstructions(). Getting them to a model is the application's job.

icons.notes: The wire schemas carry icons on tools, prompts, resources and Implementation, and the parsed results hand them to the application. The SDK renders nothing.

tasks.notes: No task runtime in either era. The 2025-11-25 related-task _meta key is marked as kept for interoperability only, with no SDK runtime. The 2026-07-28 wire registry has no tasks/* methods. HEAD (after 2.4.0) adds ClientOptions.extensions, through which an application could supply a tasks extension; the SDK ships none.

jsonSchema.notes: On Node the default validator is Ajv with formats, picked by the schema's $schema: none or 2020-12 uses Ajv2020, 2019-09 uses Ajv2019, draft-07 and draft-06 use classic Ajv. Other dialects fail to compile and callTool throws before sending. Browser and workerd builds use @cfworker/json-schema. jsonSchemaValidator replaces it.

io.modelcontextprotocol/skills.notes: SkillsClient from @modelcontextprotocol/client/ext/skills wraps a connected Client and reads the server's skills (SEP-2640). It does not add anything to the client's declared capabilities. Present in 2.4.0.

io.modelcontextprotocol/ui.notes: No MCP Apps code in packages/client or packages/core-internal.

protocolEraForcing.notes: versionNegotiation takes legacy (the default), auto, or { pin: '2026-07-28' }. connect({ prior }) reuses a cached era verdict with no probe. supportedProtocolVersions narrows both lists.

standardRequestHeaders.notes: Only on a 2026-07-28 connection over HTTP: Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name on every request, and Mcp-Param-* mirrored from x-mcp-header input-schema declarations of a cached tool. Skipped in a browser.

listChanged.notes: With ClientOptions.listChanged set, connect opens a subscriptions/listen stream for the advertised list types. Without it nothing is subscribed.

subscribe.notes: listen() opens subscriptions/listen with a filter. It throws on a 2025 connection.

elicitation.notes: Server requests arrive as input_required results on tools/call, prompts/get or resources/read. By default the client answers them through the handler registered for elicitation/create, sampling/createMessage or roots/list and retries the call, up to 10 rounds. With no handler the call fails. An inbound server-to-client request is dropped.

evidence.note: An input_required round with no registered handler for the embedded method fails with CapabilityNotSupported.
